note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 117, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: The existing French colonial empire Q179023 is not an unambiguous identity for Napoleon’s army at Austerlitz. Both source forces remain local; the Russian/Austrian Allied total is not split.

Equipment review: the source-named FR ARMY retains its complete CDB90 aggregate and all strength and loss estimates. A cocked-hat infantryman with a Model 1777-style flintlock and socket bayonet illustrates one documented French infantry equipment component. Contemporary dress and weapons varied; the model does not establish the uniform, firearm type or troop composition of every soldier, nor represent cavalry, artillery or attached contingents. Identity evidence is recorded separately from the museum equipment sources. The assignment uses the 1804–1805 Imperial profile; no shako is introduced before 1806.
